ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Evel Knievel

code.originalText: End of 12 weeks of antiviral treatment: liver tests, glucose monitoring in cirrhosis, osteoporosis, pain, and abstinence

text.paragraph: End of 12 weeks of hepatitis C treatment. [S]

Mr. Knievel finished sofosbuvir-velpatasvir yesterday without missing a dose. He has had no alcohol since the day treatment started. He takes carvedilol 12.5 mg daily without dizziness. His glucose sensor has shown no readings below 70 mg/dL. The bone density scan ten weeks ago showed osteoporosis at the hip. He has had no falls since starting physical therapy, walks 20 minutes on flat ground and swims twice a week; pain is about 4 of 10. He has not yet had his diabetic eye examination because the appointment was not booked after the referral. He saw his dentist last week. He has had no muscle aches, abdominal swelling, black stools, confusion or yellow eyes. He has had no thoughts of self-harm. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-05-18; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 83.2 kg; blood pressure 118/72, pulse 62
No asterixis; gait steady with a cane

Raised transaminases (ALT 88, AST 96 U/L) and low platelets (118) on today's tests, with spider angiomas and palmar erythema, in a man of 57 who received many blood transfusions after crashes before 1992 and drinks most evenings: chronic liver disease, most likely hepatitis C, must be excluded. Hepatitis C antibody with reflex RNA, hepatitis A and B serology, HIV, liver ultrasound and hepatology review ordered
S — Synthetic presenting problem; no symptom or result of his real illness was made public. Superseded at the hepatology consultation.

Chronic hepatitis C, genotype 1a, treatment-naive, HCV RNA 2.35 million IU/mL, likely acquired through blood transfusions after crashes; synthetic modern detail linked to his publicly reported transfusion-acquired hepatitis C
S — Synthetic genotype, viral load and timing; his hepatitis C and its likely transfusion source are documented (D).

Compensated cirrhosis from hepatitis C, with alcohol as a cofactor: liver stiffness 26.8 kPa, FIB-4 4.94, nodular liver and a 14.2 cm spleen on ultrasound, platelets 118; Child-Pugh A5, MELD-Na 8; no ascites, encephalopathy, jaundice or bleeding
S — Synthetic stage of liver disease linked to his documented hepatitis C and later liver transplant.
Clinically significant portal hypertension in compensated cirrhosis (liver stiffness 25 kPa or more), treated with carvedilol without screening endoscopy (Baveno VII)
S — Synthetic finding at the hepatology consultation.
S — Synthetic; diabetes is documented only in his last years (D), and placing it at 57 is a synthetic choice.
Chronic pain in the back, hips, pelvis and knees after dozens of fractures from stunt crashes, including a broken pelvis; ibuprofen stopped, and managed without oral NSAIDs or opioids
S — Synthetic pain at the index age, anchored to his documented fractures and the pain of his later years.
Osteoporosis in a man with cirrhosis, prior heavy alcohol use and dozens of old fractures: femoral neck T-score -2.6, lumbar spine -1.9

list.item:
Chronic hepatitis C, genotype 1a, end of treatment (B18.2). Treatment completed with full adherence. HCV RNA is not detected at the end of treatment and ALT 24 and AST 29 U/L are normal; cure is confirmed only by a test 12 or more weeks from now. [S]
HCV RNA and liver tests 12 or more weeks after the last dose, with the six-month ultrasound.

Osteoporosis (M81.8). Femoral neck T-score -2.6 with a 10-year hip fracture risk of 4.1% in a man with cirrhosis, prior heavy alcohol use and dozens of old fractures: treatment is indicated. Secondary causes are addressed: vitamin D now 34 ng/mL, calcium 9.3 mg/dL, parathyroid hormone 48 pg/mL and testosterone 455 ng/dL are normal. An oral bisphosphonate can irritate the esophagus, which is a concern with portal hypertension and possible varices, so a yearly zoledronic acid infusion is preferred. His dental check is done. [S]
Zoledronic acid 5 mg intravenously in two weeks.
Calcium from food about 1000 mg a day; continue vitamin D3.
Bone density again in two years.

Type 2 diabetes in cirrhosis (E11.65). A1c 6.4% but a glucose management indicator of 6.9%: the A1c reads lower than the true average, as it can in cirrhosis, so the sensor guides treatment. No hypoglycemia on metformin as the virus cleared. [S]
Continue metformin and the sensor.
Eye examination booked today for next month.

Clinically significant portal hypertension (K76.6). Pulse 62 and blood pressure 118/72 on carvedilol 12.5 mg. [S]
Continue carvedilol.

Vitamin D deficiency (E55.9). Vitamin D 34 ng/mL after replacement; resolved. [S]
Continue vitamin D3 2000 units daily.

Chronic pain from old fractures (G89.29). 4 of 10; walking 20 minutes; no NSAIDs or opioids. [S]
Continue aquatic therapy and the home program.

Next scheduled visit 2026-08-17: cure confirmed (SVR12): six-month liver cancer surveillance, cirrhosis care after cure, and transplant criteria reviewed. [S]
